questions.background: Berlin is both a city and a German federal state. Its state election determines the composition of its parliament.

questions.title: Which sector will show the largest year-on-year percentage decline in Iran's official GDP report for March 21–June 20, 2026?
questions.background: Iran is at war with the United States and Israel.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Statistical Center of Iran's GDP figures for March 21–June 20, 2026, publicly reported by September 21, 2026. The answer is the economic sector with the greatest year-on-year percentage contraction among the sectors reported. Resolution Date : 2026-09-21 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the sector's conventional name.

That directly invalidates Water and electricity (previously 0.12) and sharply downgrades Industry (previously 0.16), removing both from the top 5 while retaining residual probability (~0.06 combined) in case Statistical Center of Iran's final report diverges from preliminary/CBI figures. Meanwhile, Sept 13 Al Jazeera reporting underscores severe wartime contraction in investment, housing, hospitality/dining, and air/sea/overland transit amid 89% August inflation (127% food) and the maritime blockade. Because smaller-weight sectors can suffer deep double-digit contractions consistent with mild -0.21% headline GDP, Construction (already plunging -15.8% in FY 1404 and -33.0% in Q3 1404) rises to #1 at 0.28 (up from 0.22), Oil and gas trims slightly 0.28 -> 0.24 (Hormuz/war disruption offset by mild headline contraction and pre-July-14 blockade timing), Accommodation and food jumps 0.06 -> 0.14 (already -20.3% in Q4 1404 with wartime Nowruz travel wipeout), Transportation and storage enters at 0.10 (airspace/shipping/rail chokepoints), and Agriculture enters at 0.07 (drought/input shock; top-5 sum = 0.83, leaving 0.17 for Industry, Mining, Trade, Real estate, Water/electricity, and other SCI subsectors).
